title: Officer Fires After Suspect Advances With Boxcutter
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
Queens, N.Y. — On Sunday, December 21, 2025, at approximately 12:29 a.m., Officer Pointdujour and her partner, Officer Amanda Delarosa, responded to a 911 call at a residential building in the vicinity of Central Avenue and Nameoke Street, for a dispute involving 29-year-old Chez Fray and another person. The 911 caller reported that Fray was acting violent, however denied that he possessed a weapon. Upon arrival, the officers met with the 911 caller and another civilian witness, who escorted them to the apartment where Fray was believed to have been located. When Officer Pointdujour and Officer Delarosa arrived at the apartment, they searched for Fray with the 911 caller and discovered that he was not inside. Fray then appeared in the hallway of the location and was in possession of a boxcutter in his right hand. 

While the officers ordered Fray several times to drop his weapon, the 911 caller intervened, causing a physical dispute between Fray and the 911 caller. During the dispute, Fray maintained possession of the boxcutter. The officers ordered the 911 caller several times to move out of their way, however he refused to do so and began to physically grapple with Fray. After approximately 35 seconds of grappling, the 911 caller broke off from Fray and ran towards Officer Pointdujour and Officer Delarosa. As the 911 caller ran towards the officers, Fray followed him while in possession of the boxcutter. As Fray ran towards the 911 caller and the officers, Officer Delarosa deployed her Taser Conducted Electrical Weapon at him. Fray continued to move forward at which point, Officer Pointdujour discharged two rounds from her service firearm, striking Fray. Fray was taken into custody and transported via ambulance to Jamaica Hospital Medical Center where he was pronounced deceased.
